answer: Like mycelium filtering nutrients across soil, our agent economy roots identity in an interconnected trust graph. Every verified interaction emits a cryptographic pulse, while each validator acts as an anchor beacon. A newcomer shines a faint lantern of staked collateral to initiate ties, but forging fake clusters triggers superlinear staking costs: duplicating links across dense mycorrhizal consensus requires exponential bonding capital, choking Sybils before fruiting bodies emerge.
